title: Harness MCP allocates root correlation and propagates it into local worker execution
summary: Harness MCP tools/call now allocates one correlation_id at dispatch, records MCP START/DONE/ERROR, carries trace metadata into browser commands, passes correlation into local_exec_start child environments, and allows run-task-envelope to reuse the same correlation for TERM→OC→QWEN→LLAMA. Detailed OpenCode tool/model events inherit the same context from event-context.json.
claims: MCP tool calls create a root span before tool execution.
local_exec_start exposes EDH_CORRELATION_ID and EDH_PARENT_SPAN_ID to its child process.
run-task-envelope reuses an upstream correlation and parents its TERM span to the MCP tool span.
OpenCode tool_use, step_finish and QWEN text events can inherit worker correlation from event-context.json.
The current ChatGPT Web session still does not provide transport-observed conversation/turn/message identity to Harness.
decision: Treat MCP-root correlation propagation as implemented and tested; keep OBS-04/GW-01 open until a live Harness client proves MCP→TERM→OC→QWEN→LLAMA on one correlation and ChatGPT turn/message identity is transport-observed rather than declared.
rationale: Correlation must be allocated before dispatch and carried by source-owned metadata, not reconstructed later by timestamp heuristics.

evidence.note: MCP tools/call emits one START/DONE correlation and passes trace to browser command.
local_exec_start propagates correlation metadata through child environment.
Task envelope reuses upstream MCP correlation when present.
OC read/write/step and QWEN CRITICAL events inherit corr:30b0bf97-d535-4f6b-a41a-43f9df816d01 from event-context.json.
